title: Day 759: Army Pursuit Ends in Gunfight in Angostura — Two Civilians Killed, One Detained
detail: On the afternoon of Friday, August 21, 2026, Mexican Army personnel pursued an armed group of civilians traveling in a vehicle near the municipal baseball stadium in Angostura, the coastal municipality's seat. Accounts vary on the vehicle (a black Chevrolet Tahoe or a gray Ford pickup), which crashed into a home on or near Macario Gaxiola Street during the chase, causing structural damage. An exchange of gunfire followed; two civilians were killed and a third was detained by Army personnel. Firearms, magazines and cartridges were secured at the scene as judicial authorities opened an investigation.

media.caption: Scene of the Army-civilian gunfight in Angostura, Sinaloa, August 21, 2026

title: Day 759: Four More Killed Across Culiacán, Navolato and the Mazatlán Highway
detail: Beyond the Angostura clash, Friday, August 21, 2026 brought four more homicides across Sinaloa. In Culiacán, two men were shot dead on Avenida Aquiles Serdán in the Miguel Alemán neighborhood by attackers on a motorcycle who fled the scene. In Navolato, Julián Rosario 'N', 44, a shellfish harvester from the El Castillo fishing camp, was executed at the 'La Curva' bend near the old highway in the San Pedro township; his bullet-riddled gray Chevrolet Tornado was secured as evidence. On the Mazatlán–Culiacán highway near El Recreo, the body of a man with multiple gunshot wounds was found on a bridge. No arrests were reported in any of the three incidents.

media.caption: Shellfish harvester Julián Rosario 'N' executed at the San Pedro curve, Navolato, August 21, 2026

title: Day 759: Rocha Moya Defies US Chapitos Allegations, Resumes Sinaloa Governorship After 112-Day Leave
detail: Rubén Rocha Moya resumed his post as Governor of Sinaloa on August 21, 2026, ending a 112-day leave he had requested May 1 to respond to US Department of Justice accusations — conspiracy to traffic drugs, bribery, and institutional protection of Los Chapitos — filed in the April 29-30 SDNY indictment that also targeted nine other officials. Announcing his return on social media, Rocha said he came back 'con la frente limpia y en alto' ('with a clean, raised forehead') and 'as an ordinary citizen, without relying on constitutional immunity,' asserting Mexico's FGR found no evidence to support the US charges. Mexico's Interior Secretariat (Segob) and his own Morena party both publicly distanced themselves, calling the return a 'personal decision' rather than one backed by the federal government; Segob said the US had still not answered its repeated requests for supporting evidence. A US State Department spokesperson responded the same day that the Sinaloa Cartel 'could not operate without the help of corrupt officials.' Rocha's term runs through October 31, 2027; critics questioned whether resuming office now shields him with gubernatorial immunity (fuero) from further prosecution.

media.caption: Rubén Rocha Moya resumes the Sinaloa governorship, August 21, 2026
